steps.title: Welcome, coder
steps.body: Game rules in Brick Worlds are logic: when something happens (an event), do something (actions). You can build them as a node graph or write them as code — a small, safe dialect of JavaScript. Both are the same thing: edit one and the other follows. This course teaches the code, line by line, in a sandbox with a generated map.

steps.title: Set the stage
steps.body: The lessons need a few things on the map: a treasure chest, a trigger zone (a pond), a reward scene and a variable named coins. Do it for me places them, or press Next if you want to place them yourself first (Assets › Treasure chest, the Trigger zone tool Z, Cinematics › New reward scene, Logic › Variables).
steps.task: Place a chest, a zone and a reward scene (or let me).

steps.title: A graph to write in
steps.body: Open Logic. Each graph holds event blocks; this course writes into one graph called “Coding course”. Then switch the editor to Code with the View buttons (Graph · Code · Split).
steps.task: Open the Coding course graph in the Code view.
steps.tip: Split shows the graph and the code side by side.

steps.title: Anatomy of a block
steps.body: Every block starts with on("event", …) and a function (e) => { … }. Inside the braces go statements, one per line, each ending with a semicolon. The e gives you details about what happened (e.who for a zone). Lines starting with // are comments.
steps.task: Look at the empty on("start") block, then press Next.

steps.title: Your first line
steps.body: log(value) writes to the Console (the dock's Console tab) while playing. Put it inside the start block: it runs once when the game starts.
steps.task: Type the log line inside on("start").
steps.tip: The editor turns your text into the graph a moment after you stop typing.

steps.title: Run it
steps.body: Press Play (F5). The start block runs and the Console shows “Logic: Hello, bricks!”. Nothing you do while playing changes the project.
steps.task: Press Play and find your message in the Console.

steps.title: Stop
steps.body: Stop returns to the editor exactly as it was.
